$comment: Real customer reviews of The Wire Guy Electric, copied verbatim (text, name, rating and date exactly as displayed) from the BrightLocal "Showcase Reviews" widget embedded on the live site. Nothing here is edited, shortened, combined or invented. Imported by scripts/migrate/content/reviews.mjs as one Sanity "review" document per review, except entries with excludedFromSanity.

widget.embeddedOnLivePagesNote: Checked by fetching each live page for the embed (2026-10-13). Not found on /about-us, /contact-us, /services, /residential-electrician, /blog, /services/panels or /services/exterior-electrical; the discovery inventory finds it only in the home, commercial and location templates. Every embed is the same widget (id 21435), so every page shows the same 50 reviews.

business.name: The Wire Guy Electric
business.note: Business the widget is configured for, from the createLdSchema({type: "Electrician", ...}) call in the embed script (which passes no reviews: reviewCount 0, ratingValue 0, containsFirstPartyReviews false).

method: Playwright (Chromium) opened https://www.thewireguyelectric.com/, scrolled to #reviews so the lazy embed injected its iframe, scrolled the frame to the bottom, clicked every visible "Read More" (26 of 50 cards were truncated client-side at 140 characters), then read each .Review-container: star class (is-rating-N), .Review-date, directory icon, .Review-name and the full [data-target="read-more.text"] textContent.

The same 50 cards are in the iframe's server-rendered HTML (migration/reviews/brightlocal-widget-snapshot.html). Parsed with JavaScript disabled, its names, dates and full texts matched the rendered cards character for character; "Read More" only hides text client-side.

Every request the widget made: the embed script, the iframe document, one stylesheet, widget.js and four images. There is no JSON API: widget.js makes no fetch/XHR calls, the page has no pagination or "load more" control, and page/offset/limit/per_page query parameters return the same 50 reviews.
Dates are shown as MM.DD.YYYY (e.g. 02.20.2026) and stored as ISO dates.

Source platform comes from each card's directory icon (icons/google.png or icons/yahoo.png; the icon has no alt text or label). The widget shows no links at all, so Google reviews get sourceUrl = the Google Business Profile link the live site itself uses (see googleBusinessProfile).

googleBusinessProfile.linkedFrom: footer of the live blog-category pages (e.g. https://www.thewireguyelectric.com/posts-categories/industrial): "Our contacts" > "Mesa, Arizona". The footer map icon there links https://maps.app.goo.gl/6qQ2iDaf8YGrdJuW8, which resolves to the same place.
googleBusinessProfile.matchesWidgetBusiness: Same business name, and the place coordinates (33.4398269, -111.6898689) are in Mesa, the city of the address the widget is configured for.

notes: The widget header says "333 Total Reviews" but it lists only 50 reviews (newest first). It has no paging, no "load more" and no API, so the other 283 are not exposed by it.

Date range of the reviews shown: 2025-12-17 to 2026-02-26. The newest is about seven months older than this pull (2026-10-13), so the widget appears to have stopped picking up new reviews; the Google profile likely has newer ones this pull cannot see.
siteSettings.reviewSummary (from the live LocalBusiness JSON-LD) says 380 reviews, rating 5.0; the widget says 333.
Every review the widget shows is 5 stars, so the featured picks being all 5 stars is not a selection effect.

rules: Location: tagged only when the text names a served city that has a location document (matched by city name); evidence is the sentence that names it. Mesa has no location document (the homepage serves Mesa), so a Mesa mention is recorded under cityMentions only.
Service: tagged only when the text clearly describes work a specific service page covers; evidence is a verbatim phrase from the text. Generic praise ("fixed the problem") is not tagged.
Featured: 6-9 specific, recent, varied reviews (the work done, a named technician, or Emma).
Rating-only reviews (no text) would be skipped; the widget has none.

reviews.text:
I had a great experience with The Wire Guy Electric here in Tempe. They came out to fix a lighting issue and diagnosed a failed ballast. Instead of pushing a full fixture replacement, they professionally rerouted around the ballast and converted it properly so everything works safely and efficiently.

They were on time (early, in fact), explained the solution clearly, and left the area clean. The $195 charge felt very fair for the service and expertise.

If you’re looking for a reliable, licensed electrician in Mesa or the Tempe area, I highly recommend them. Honest work and no upselling--just solid electrical service.

Call 'em! =)

Update (Feb 2026): Had them come back out for a different project! Still highly recommend! 5 stars!!!

This time Blake came by to install a new outlet and was just as excellent as Rhett back in November. He was just as polite, personable and very knowledgeable.

Highly Recommend The Wire Guy Electric!

The Wire Guy Electric is officially my go-to! From my first call to my completed installation, I had an excellent experience with The Wire Guy Electric. When I called to ask about having outlets installed above my kitchen cabinets and on two other high ledges, I spoke with Emma. She was extremely friendly, helpful, and professional, and she was able to schedule an appointment for the very next week. The time window was 10–12, and the electrician Rhett called when he was on his way and arrived right at 10:00.

Rhett was polite, personable, and very knowledgeable. I explained what I needed, and he quickly assessed the situation and started working right away. He even took the time to look at what had been left on top of the cabinets by a previous owner and found a way to use what was already there. Because he didn’t have to fish a wire through the wall, it actually saved me money—which I really appreciated.

The job took a little longer than expected because one of the outlets turned out to be more involved than we thought, but Rhett answered every question I had and still managed to finish all three outlets plus a fourth one with the remaining time.

Overall, it was a great experience from start to finish. I will absolutely be using them again for more electrical work in the near future, and I will definitely be requesting Rhett.

Highly recommend The Wire Guy Electric!

reviews.text:
Just had them out again for the 4th time!  Today’s tasks were installing more pot lights in the big room and a new outlet behind the bed in guest room.  What I said the first time (below) is exactly what I’d say today. Cade and Cole were the guys today. Great job once again.

A-maz-ing work!  Everything looks like it was always there. We had them install a can light above the BBQ outside and a flood light in backyard patio area so we can see when we eat at night or play table games.  The placement was perfect. The 4 can lights in the office literally was like night and day.  The ceiling fan light was always so dim and changing the bulb made no difference.  Thank goodness we went with installation of can lights rather than replacing the ceiling fan. What an amazing difference. We had made the closet into a built-in bookshelf/filing cabinet by California Closets, but couldn't see the titles of the books. We had three can lights installed above them with the switch on the wall right outside it.  Steve, the estimator, guided us in the right direction for everything we were needing. Gave great suggestions on placement and types of lights and switches.  We had light switches that didn't go to anything and one switch that went to two things at the same time (ceiling fan & fan). Got those separated and on dimmer switches. Had dimmer switches put in several places in the house - like above the dining room table.  Soooo nice! In the broom/vacuum/ cleaning products closet they installed an overhead light that turns on when the door opens. They also installed an AC outlet for the battery charger for the stick vacuum in that closet.  We also had them put an outlet under the bathroom counter so the hair dryer could be left plugged in and hidden on a shelf.   Cody and his crew were like busy bees all day with the installations. They never even stopped for lunch.  Their work was truly great and they cleaned up afterward. They all seemed to like working together and enjoyed their work.  The attic situation made some installations challenging but Cody figured out workarounds.  His problem solving skills and suggestions were right on target. Before going ahead with outlets we wanted higher up on a couple of walls, he stopped and explained that he'd have to cut through the drywall to go horizontally above our desk. We then decided not to do those. There are a few places where it was necessary to cut drywall but they are mostly in hidden spots. We will be using their older brother who does drywall repair.

This is a family business and even the receptionist is Steven’s fiancé. The communication by phone, verbally, and via text was very good. They were timely, precise, and professional. You really couldn’t ask for more from an electrician outfit. We loved everything they did so much that we just had them out to do more!

HIGHLY recommend!

reviews.text:
For some reason the power going to our custom built-in entertainment center went out. The circuit breaker had popped, but when I flipped it back on the power didn't come back on.

That was the extent of my electrical know-how. I actually replaced the breaker as a hail Mary prayer to try and fix it, but that didn't do anything.

I found The Wire Guys on Offer Up. Short version: they fixed everything. I got a bill. I thought for sure they had made a mistake because it was far far less than I expected, so I called them to fix it. I told them if that was the correct price, I wanted them to text me links to everywhere they wanted me to leave a review. It was correct and now I'm leaving this review.

I could not believe that the young guy I had been dealing with was the owner. What a great thing to see, someone that age making good money and doing a damn good job at it.

I have since referred my sister to them so they could diagnose and fix the awful job her electrician did (that resulted in a small fire) and she was super happy with them as well.

I'm leaving this review about 8 months after the fact, but good karma is always welcome, so that's what I'm creating here.

Thanks y'all
